<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **100** documentable anchor(s).

**63** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 39 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **246** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **181** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **181**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **122** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bfe6a30105c9575241eb15284cef19f49f234266` — the merge of head `2850beca7b5436ce199cebb52e19c655131917ab` into base `f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bfe6a30105c9575241eb15284cef19f49f234266 && git checkout bfe6a30105c9575241eb15284cef19f49f234266
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341 2850beca7b5436ce199cebb52e19c655131917ab && git checkout -B drift-repro f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341 && git merge --no-ff 2850beca7b5436ce199cebb52e19c655131917ab

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6385839bb4b90d400e1ee6e14d108a236461cc5e`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: no `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path (`check-governed-merges --pr 32268`: 0 of 37 paths; +2646/-76 = 2722 ≤ 3000, Tier S).
- What widens: `sys_sso_provider` gains two declared actions (`edit_saml_provider`, `edit_oidc_provider`, platform-admin gate and `visible` as the register actions; the OIDC secret is `type: 'password'`, on the credential roster), and the delete action gains `preflight` + `resultDialog`. Two new server-only routes, both ledgered: `POST /admin/sso/update-provider` and `GET /admin/sso/delete-impact` (closed query set). The `/sso/delete-provider` answer gains a `data` member on success. All additive.
- **What narrows:** `/sso/register` (direct door and both register bridges) and a domain edit on `/sso/update-provider` now refuse `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` (`field: 'domain'`) for an exact domain entry another provider already serves. That request succeeded before this PR. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 a refusal of a request that used to succeed is the `(narrowing)` arm, which is BREAKING, whatever the merit (the second provider was unreachable by address; the seat ruled refuse, not warn). The delete door also gains a new `503` when its count cannot be read: same class, new refusal on an existing door.
- Kept: no existing row is touched by the domain rule (a self re-save is admitted, pinned); subdomain-beside-parent stays accepted both ways (pinned); the vendor's own provider-access and identity-while-linked refusals still run.

### ② Semver level

`Metadata-protocol: none` → **patch** on both packages (step 3: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`), as the changeset declares. The declaration lines are what is wrong, not the level.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Declaration mismatch (blocking):** the PR body and the changeset say `Clause-②: yes` with no arm. The narrowing above makes it `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. The fault is the seat's: the order and claim 6766299848 carried `yes` without the arm, and the dev copied it as told. A correction to the claim follows this review.
- What the arm carries: `!` in the PR title; a BREAKING banner and exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker in the changeset body (`check:adr-0087-registration` prints the categories); a `Skills-docs:` line per the claim template; the full dogfood battery on the final head, recorded as `dogfood_battery` (review checklist: missing ⇒ no queue).
- Census: two new engine write sites, recorded by `tenant-audit-census.mjs --write` (295 at the merged head).
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay `pr_create`).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-2fhict`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufziCTpjnYbdh76SAWwb`

**VERDICT: REVISE** — declarations and the obligations of the `(narrowing)` arm only; no code change asked. A re-review on the new head follows the patch round.

### ① Derived judgments

Requests that succeeded before this PR and are refused on this head:

1. `POST /sso/register` naming a domain entry another provider already lists: `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `field: 'domain'`. Declared. Right.
2. The same through `POST /admin/sso/register` and `/admin/sso/register-saml`, which relay it with `code: RESOURCE_CONFLICT` instead of `SSO_REGISTER_FAILED` / `SAML_REGISTER_FAILED`. Declared. Right.
3. `POST /sso/update-provider` with a `domain` that collides with another provider's entry: the same `409`. Declared. Right.
4. `POST /sso/delete-provider` when the impact count cannot be read: `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, nothing deleted. Declared. Right.
5. `POST /sso/register` and a domain edit on `/sso/update-provider` when the provider table cannot be read for the collision check: `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (`assertSsoProviderDomainFree`, the `catch` arm). **Not declared.** The changeset and the PR body name the `503` on delete only. Same class as 4, so the `(narrowing)` arm already covers it; the sentence that lists the refusals is one short (nit N1).

So `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right declaration and covers all five; its prose names four.

Not narrowed, checked: a provider re-saving its own domain (the row is excluded by `providerId`), a subdomain beside its parent in either order, every update that carries no `domain`, a delete with no data engine wired (nothing staged, vendor answer unchanged), and every stored provider (nothing re-checks a row at boot or on read).

Widened, all additive: two `sys_sso_provider` actions (`edit_saml_provider`, `edit_oidc_provider`), `preflight` and `resultDialog` on `delete_sso_provider` (its `successMessage` goes, which `resultDialog` supersedes per `action.zod.ts`), two ledgered server-only routes (`POST /admin/sso/update-provider`, `GET /admin/sso/delete-impact`), a `data` member on a successful `/sso/delete-provider` answer, and `field` / `heldBy` on the register bridges' error. No `packages/spec` path, no package export and no stored key changes.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch` on both packages (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3). The changeset declares `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/platform-objects`. Right.
- `!` in the PR title: present (`feat(plugin-auth)!:`). The changeset's own title line carries it too.
- BREAKING banner in the changeset body: present.
- ADR-0087 disposition marker: exactly one, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. It fits: no authorable key moves.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`: line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset, and they agree with claim correction 6771602670.
- `Skills-docs:` line: present in the PR body, `none`. Verified: no file under `skills/` names `sso/register`, `delete-provider`, `register_sso_provider` or an SSO provider.
- **Dogfood battery on the final head: NOT met (must-fix M1).** The battery ran at `488ec59b`. The head is `2850beca`, which merges six further commits from `main` (88 files, +4993) and got targeted re-runs only. The review checklist pins the battery to the head and reads a narrowed one as missing. The PR's own `Dogfood Regression Gate` check is `success` with its three shards `skipped`, as PR runs always are, so it does not stand in. The card's posted `os-dev-report` (6771402035) still records `dogfood_battery: n/a`; the round-2 value exists only in the dev's report file.

Gate verdicts on this head at review time. `success`: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint · ESLint, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped (tooling self-tests, query-options erasure, slot lookup & corpus), Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Build Docs, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size. **Still running, no verdict:** Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates. The tests that pin this PR live in `Test Core`, so their verdict on this head is not in.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The head cannot merge.** GitHub reports `mergeable: false` (`dirty`). `main` at `60b99f8f` conflicts with it in `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md` (#32208 added census sites). Resolving it moves the head, and this record does not cover the new one. The battery M1 asks for belongs on that head.
- **Refuse versus warn on a served domain is not ruled on the card.** The card's Expected offers "refused or warned". The seat ruling in claim 6766299848 covers delete only; "refuse, not warn" appears in the PR body alone. Escalated with S1 below: it needs the seat's ruling recorded on the card.
- Dev deviations, each answered:
  - Files outside the order's surface (`platform-objects.test.ts` roster row, the two census files, the two dogfood sweeps): accepted. Each is what a gate or the battery demands for the new routes, param and write sites.
  - "Assign and request review" skipped, and the commit trailer without a model name: accepted, both follow repo rules that outrank the harness step.
  - `main` merged six times; the #32188 conflicts kept both sides: checked in ④, coherent.
  - `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` exit 3 on a shallow clone: environment, not this diff.
  - `check-closing-target-claim` UNDETERMINED on the claim's `Branch:` line: the seat's line to fix (the parenthetical after the branch in 6766299848). The PR-body guards check is `success` on this head.
- `open_questions`: none.
- security: one finding routed privately

### ④ Design judgment

**`sso-provider-lifecycle.ts` and the delete door (`auth-manager.ts`, both hooks).** Holds. The count is staged after the held-caller refusal and the sign-in method floor and before the vendor writes. It is stashed on the per-request context and removed before use. Cleanup runs only when the vendor answered `success: true`, so a `403` or `404` removes nothing and carries no counts. Grants are selected by exact equality with `ssoGroupProjectionReason(providerId)`, the same marker `reconcileMappedGrants` and `revokeSsoProjectedGrants` use, and each is deleted with its own organization as tenant, as the sibling in `idp-group-mapping-admin.ts` does. Mappings are selected by `source_kind: 'sso'` and `source_id`. No default row cap sits on `engine.find`, so the counts and the cleanup are whole. A failed cleanup is said in the answer and once at `error` with the remedy.

- **S1 (should-fix): the domain refusal's stated reason does not hold for every provider it refuses.** The message and the changeset say a second provider on a served domain "could never be reached". `sys_sso_provider` declares `allow_idp_initiated`: an IdP-initiated SAML sign-in reaches a provider through its own ACS URL with no address routing. That is the card's own setup (`okta-saml` beside `okta-oidc` on one domain). With delete unlinking every user and no console door for a domain edit, moving one domain from SAML to OIDC now means deleting the old provider first. The card permits a refusal, so this is not a must-fix; it needs the seat's ruling on the card naming that case, and the refusal message and changeset sentence corrected to "by address".
- **S2 (should-fix): `usersWithoutOtherSignIn` counts account rows, not usable sign-in methods.** A linked user who also holds a `credential` row is counted as keeping access. With email and password switched off for the deployment (the state `sign-in-method-floor.ts` exists for), that user loses access and the confirmation says they do not. The label ("Users who lose access") and the sentence ("lose access") state more than the read knows. Either consult the same facts the floor reads, or word the count as what it is (no password and no other provider linked).
- **N1 (nit, prose):** the changeset's refusal list omits the `503` of ① item 5.
- **N2 (nit):** a provider listing a subdomain inside a multi-entry list (`eng.acme.com, foo.com`) beside one for the parent is accepted, yet by the diff's own account of vendor routing (exact whole-value match first, else the first list match, subdomains included) the parent can win `eng.acme.com`. The pinned control covers the single-entry shape only. Follow-up card.
- **N3 (nit):** the collision read is check-then-write with no unique index on `domain`, so two concurrent registers can both pass. Entries are compared after URL parsing while the store is narrowed by the raw substring, so an internationalised domain stored in Unicode is not matched by its punycode form. Follow-up card.

**`register-sso-provider.ts` (edit bridge, delete-impact read, relay).** Holds. The bridge sends only changed members and never `mapping`; ablations A14 and A15 pin that. The client secret goes through the adapter's `update`, where `liftClientSecretForWrite` runs on the patch (`objectql-adapter.ts`), so it is stored as on register; the test reads it back through the adapter. The answer names fields, never values. A field of the other protocol, an OIDC issuer change, a non-X.509 certificate and an empty edit are refused `400` before the vendor is called. The delete-impact read has a closed query set and answers `404` for an unknown provider.

- **N4 (nit):** certificate rotation and `keepCurrentCert` are pinned by what is stored (`cert` as a string or a list), not by a signed assertion accepted under the new or the second certificate. That the vendor verifies against a stored list is the diff's measurement, not a test.
- **N5 (nit):** `keepCurrentCert: 'false'` as text on an OIDC provider is read as a SAML field and refused; only the boolean `false` is exempt.

**`auth-plugin.ts`, `auth-route-ledger.ts`.** Holds. Both routes call `gateAdmin` first, ahead of any body or query read, and reuse `readSsoProviderConfigs` and `handleWithTransportOf` from the #32188 block. Both ledger rows are `server-only` and describe what the handlers do.

**The #32188 merge.** Coherent. The register bridges keep `mappingWithAttributes` and `mappingWithGroupsClaim` beside `registerRefusal`. `set-attribute-mapping` and `set-groups-claim` re-dispatch the whole stored mapping; the new edit door sends none, so neither overwrites the other. The action roster carries the four #32188 actions and the two new ones with distinct names and targets. No conflict marker in any file of the diff.

**`sys-sso-provider.object.ts`.** Holds against `action.zod.ts`: `preflight` sits on an action with non-empty `params`, its read is a same-origin `GET` with a `ctx.record.FIELD` hole, and its fields use the shared `text` format. `clientSecret` is `type: 'password'` with no `defaultFromRow`, and is on the credential roster. Both edit actions carry the platform-admin gate and `visible`, and no `ai` block.

**Tests and sweeps.** `sso-provider-lifecycle.test.ts` runs a real engine, `AuthManager`, `sso()` plugin and route registration; providers are stored directly, not registered through the vendor, except in the register cases. `admin-sso-bridge-gate.test.ts` covers anonymous, member, org admin and position-named callers on both doors. The two dogfood sweeps classify both routes like their siblings. Their verdict on this head is the pending `Test Core`.

Delta owed: M1 on the final head, then S1 and S2. N1 can ride the same prose edit; N2 to N5 are follow-up cards or accepted deviations.
